headline: Investor Michael Burry warns that much AI infrastructure spending may never be recovered.
score_reason: A prominent investor's opinion from a blog post, not a finding; pool score 6 kept.
importance_line: It matters most to investors in AI stocks and to the companies spending on data centres, since this is one prominent bearish view, though it is opinion from a blog post and Burry gave no detail on what 'compression' means.
summary: Our 29 Sep edition carried a CNBC report that investor Michael Burry, known for betting against the US housing market before 2008, now thinks the AI bubble may burst sooner than he first expected. Now StockTwits reports that in a Substack post he wrote that much AI spending may become "sunk cost", money that cannot be recovered, as he expects compression to make some AI investments uneconomic, that OpenAI and Anthropic want to join the oligopoly of Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Meta, a "want, not a need", and that the market could face a sizable correction in the coming months.
notes: Source is StockTwits: the Yahoo Finance copy says it was 'originally published on StockTwits'. The link is the Yahoo Finance page where the text was read; no StockTwits link was in the copy. Opinion piece, not a finding.
